Remove both to eliminate ambiguity
Treat hot-swap support as permission to ignore member identity
Hold and reconcile physical/controller identity, then correct and confirm the target
explanations: Incorrect. The conflict is a critical identity exception.
Incorrect. That worsens the degraded state.
Incorrect. Hot-swap capability does not preserve data if the wrong member is removed.
Correct. Removing the healthy member can exceed remaining tolerance.
questions.exhibit: Synthetic array: RAID5 degraded; failed serial D3/bay3; healthy serial D4/bay4; work order mistakenly names bay4. Current mapping requires confirmation.

questions.prompt: A component has a front pull handle. What can be inferred about hot replacement?
options: Every handled component requires a full building shutdown
The handle proves that all redundancy prerequisites are satisfied
Nothing definitive without the model-specific supported method and state
Every handled component can be replaced while powered
explanations: Incorrect. The actual procedure determines the scope.
Incorrect. Physical design does not report current system state.
Correct. Accessibility does not establish safe hot-swap support.
Incorrect. That is an unsafe generalization.

questions.prompt: Before a supported PSU-module replacement, which capacity check matters?
options: Only the replacement PSU nominal rating
The surviving supply and path can support the required load in the approved state
Only the sum of both PSU labels
Only idle power from a different workload
explanations: Incorrect. The remaining unit and upstream path must carry the workload during removal.
Correct. Redundancy depends on actual remaining capacity.
Incorrect. One unit will be absent during the operation.
Incorrect. It may not represent the required state.

questions.prompt: A replacement FRU has unverified firmware prerequisites. What is the appropriate disposition?
options: Hold use until the supported combination is established
Insert it and force any available update afterward
Count it as accepted because the connector matches
Erase the prerequisite note from the work order
explanations: Correct. Mechanical fit does not resolve firmware requirements.
Incorrect. That bypasses prerequisite review.
Incorrect. Connector fit is incomplete compatibility evidence.
Incorrect. That hides the unresolved condition.

questions.prompt: A removed drive contains service data. Which additional process applies?
options: Unrestricted return to general spare stock
Assume removal electrically erases all content
Use the failed-status label as a sanitization certificate
Controlled media custody and the approved return/sanitization disposition
explanations: Incorrect. Data and fault state remain relevant.
Incorrect. Persistent media retains data without power.
Incorrect. Fault status is not sanitization evidence.
Correct. Replacement does not automatically remove data obligations.

questions.prompt: What does a completed physical insertion establish by itself?
options: Correct firmware and configuration on every part
Successful independent backup restoration
The part has been installed, while recognition, function and restored protection still need verification
Full end-to-end service restoration
explanations: Incorrect. Those need read-back evidence.
Incorrect. That is a separate test.
Correct. Seating is earlier than repair acceptance.
Incorrect. That requires further checks.

questions.prompt: An unexpected alarm appears during a planned replacement outside the method's permitted conditions. What should the operator do?
options: Expand the work scope without recording it
Use the defined stop/hold process and coordinate the state
Continue faster to finish before review
Suppress the alarm permanently and proceed
explanations: Incorrect. Unreviewed scope changes can create additional risk.
Correct. Unexpected conditions invalidate assumptions of the method.
Incorrect. Speed does not resolve the changed state.
Incorrect. That conceals evidence.

questions.prompt: An accelerator class is unavailable for supervised physical practice. How is its practical requirement recorded?
options: Open until suitable authorized evidence is obtained
Completed because another component was replaced
Completed after viewing an unrelated photograph
Removed from the curriculum without review
explanations: Correct. Analytical understanding does not demonstrate that physical task.
Incorrect. Different handling and service methods need their own evidence.
Incorrect. That does not show the learner's execution.
Incorrect. Access limits do not erase mandatory outcomes.

questions.prompt: A replacement NIC links correctly but its new WWN is not authorized by the storage target. What is the next supported action?
options: Replace the NIC again before checking access policy
Copy an unrelated host's WWN without review
Declare all storage media corrupted from the denial
Verify and apply the controlled identity mapping, then test storage function
explanations: Incorrect. The new identity explains a plausible configuration failure.
Incorrect. That can create identity conflicts and unauthorized access.
Incorrect. Authorization failure does not establish media corruption.
Correct. Link state does not establish target authorization.
questions.exhibit: Synthetic replacement: link negotiated as required; new WWN=NEW01; approved target mapping still permits OLD01 only.

questions.prompt: A memory repair leaves half the expected usable capacity while the OS boots. What is the disposition?
options: Change the written capacity requirement after the fact
Assume the workload will never use the missing memory
Hold repair acceptance and verify population, recognition and mode
Accept because any successful boot proves full capacity
explanations: Incorrect. That hides the failed criterion.
Incorrect. The requirement was not conditional on that guess.
Correct. The capacity requirement is unmet.
Incorrect. Booting is insufficient.

questions.prompt: A rebuild indicator reaches 100%. What still needs review?
options: A guarantee that no future drive can fail
Terminal result, errors, protection state, integrity and service behavior
Only the displayed percentage again
Only whether the replacement drive appears in inventory
explanations: Incorrect. No rebuild can provide that guarantee.
Correct. Progress percentage alone is incomplete acceptance.
Incorrect. Repeating it adds no new mechanism evidence.
Incorrect. Recognition does not establish a successful rebuild and restored protection.

questions.prompt: ECC errors continue at the same location after a supported DIMM replacement. What should change in the diagnosis?
options: Reconsider channel/controller/connection/firmware causes with the OEM method
Conclude that the new DIMM must always be defective
Erase the location information to start fresh
Assume ECC has stopped functioning because errors are reported
explanations: Correct. Repeated part replacement without discrimination is weak evidence.
Incorrect. Other causes remain plausible.
Incorrect. That removes a key correlation.
Incorrect. Reporting does not imply the protection mechanism is absent.

questions.prompt: A replaced fan spins but its feedback is not recognized. What is missing?
options: Proof of any rotor movement
Only the fan's visible rotation speed
A claim that all spinning fans are interchangeable
Supported control/telemetry behavior and the required thermal verification
explanations: Incorrect. That was observed.
Incorrect. Visible motion does not prove recognized feedback or supported control.
Incorrect. Compatibility and control differ.
Correct. Mechanical motion alone is not the full function.

questions.prompt: An accelerator appears in inventory after replacement. Which test adds material acceptance evidence?
options: Only a second inventory listing after reboot
Assuming the old UUID remains valid everywhere
A bounded representative workload with output, error and limiting-state checks
Repeating only the inventory command many times
explanations: Incorrect. Enumeration remains weaker than exercising useful computation.
Incorrect. Identity can change and dependent configuration needs review.
Correct. Presence does not establish useful computation.
Incorrect. That does not exercise the workload mechanism.

questions.prompt: The original symptom persists after installing a new part. Which report is truthful?
options: The acceptance test should be removed
Replacement occurred, but repair effectiveness is not established
The fault is repaired because the part is new
The original evidence should be discarded
explanations: Incorrect. That would hide the unresolved requirement.
Correct. The service fault remains unresolved.
Incorrect. New hardware does not prove correction.
Incorrect. It is necessary for comparison.

questions.prompt: Why separate immediate repair acceptance from recurrence monitoring?
options: A short functional test and a longer trend observation support different claims
Immediate tests are never useful
Long-term monitoring automatically restores failed services
A successful short test proves recurrence is impossible
explanations: Correct. Both can be necessary for effectiveness evidence.
Incorrect. They verify the current required function.
Incorrect. It observes behavior rather than performing recovery.
Incorrect. It cannot guarantee future behavior.

questions.prompt: OS login returns at 25 minutes but the required OT function returns at 55 against a 45-minute RTO. What is the result?
options: Recovery passed at 25 minutes
The target is missed by 30 minutes
RTO cannot include application dependencies
The service target is missed by 10 minutes
explanations: Incorrect. That substitutes an earlier hardware/OS milestone.
Incorrect. 55−45 is 10, not the difference from OS login.
Incorrect. Those are part of the required service recovery.
Correct. The defined functional endpoint determines completion.
questions.exhibit: Synthetic recovery milestones: disruption t=0; OS login25min; database40min; required OT function and access controls55min; RTO45min.

questions.prompt: An encrypted backup's only key is on the failed host. What is missing?
options: More CPU cores for decryption
A declaration that encryption guarantees recovery
An approved accessible independent key-recovery route
A second encrypted copy protected only by the same unavailable key
explanations: Incorrect. Compute cannot replace unavailable key material.
Incorrect. Encryption protects data but adds a key dependency.
Correct. Backup bytes alone cannot establish restorability.
Incorrect. Duplicating ciphertext does not resolve key access.

questions.prompt: Why may an OS reinstall be insufficient after a management-plane compromise?
options: A new desktop proves that remote authority was removed
BMC or DPU firmware and identities can persist separately
An OS reinstall always replaces every firmware chip's contents
All management state exists only in application memory
explanations: Incorrect. Appearance does not validate access state.
Correct. Recovery scope must include the affected independent components.
Incorrect. It generally does not.
Incorrect. It can have independent persistence.

questions.prompt: A BMC is unavailable while the host service runs. Which recovery assumption is unsafe?
options: Any BMC reset is guaranteed non-disruptive on every platform
The management path needs separate diagnosis
The host service may remain available during diagnosis
Access and network controls can cause management symptoms
explanations: Correct. Actual semantics and dependencies are model-specific.
Incorrect. It is a distinct failing function.
Incorrect. The scenario establishes that possibility.
Incorrect. They are valid candidate causes.

questions.prompt: Two active nodes are given a cloned machine identity without review. What risk needs evaluation?
options: Guaranteed doubling of authentication resilience
Automatic independent key custody
Elimination of certificate validation requirements
Conflicting identity and unintended authority across the restored environment
explanations: Incorrect. Duplicate identities can undermine correct behavior.
Incorrect. Cloning does not establish independent recovery control.
Incorrect. Trust validation remains necessary.
Correct. Identity restoration must account for simultaneous ownership.

questions.prompt: What should a recovery test report separately?
options: Only the largest backup file size
Only the replacement component cost
Elapsed functional restoration and the recovered data point
Only the earliest successful ping
explanations: Incorrect. Size does not establish timing or point in time.
Incorrect. Cost is not recovery acceptance.
Correct. RTO-like timing and RPO-like data age are different measurements.
Incorrect. That omits data and required function.

questions.prompt: A temporary recovery account remains enabled after service restoration. Which requirement is unfinished?
options: The existence of any account on the system
Verification and removal or approved disposition of temporary authority
The fact that the OS can boot
The physical installation of the replacement
explanations: Incorrect. Authorized accounts remain necessary.
Correct. Functional recovery includes the intended access state.
Incorrect. That may already be complete.
Incorrect. That is a separate completed milestone.

questions.prompt: A lab plan deliberately withholds a recovery dependency. What is the purpose?
options: Expose and correct the plan's dependency weakness under controlled conditions
Prove that destructive production failures should be induced
Avoid documenting the missing dependency
Guarantee every other recovery dependency is sound
explanations: Correct. A successful test with every dependency present can miss this gap.
Incorrect. The exercise is bounded and authorized.
Incorrect. The finding must revise the plan.
Incorrect. One test has limited scope.

questions.prompt: The target accepted new writes after cutover, while the source stayed unchanged. What must rollback address?
options: Only redirecting the service name to the old source
Only powering on the source
The assumption that all writes are automatically copied backward
The target-only acknowledged data and supported reconciliation
explanations: Incorrect. Routing to stale data does not preserve target-only acknowledged writes.
Incorrect. Availability of stale data is not correct recovery.
Incorrect. That requires an implemented supported mechanism.
Correct. Returning to the source can lose valid transactions.
questions.exhibit: Synthetic migration: old source frozen10:00; target accepted writes10:00–10:30; fault10:30; zero acknowledged-transaction loss permitted.

questions.prompt: Old and new systems each draw 7 kW during migration against a 12 kW temporary limit. What is the result?
options: The demand is 7 kW because names refer to one service
The demand is 49 kW
The 14 kW transition exceeds the limit by 2 kW
The transition is acceptable because either final system draws 7 kW
explanations: Incorrect. Two running systems still consume power.
Incorrect. Power values are summed, not multiplied.
Correct. The simultaneous state must be checked.
Incorrect. Final-state demand does not validate overlap.

questions.prompt: Why define one authoritative write owner during cutover?
options: A shared hostname automatically coordinates all writes
Uncoordinated concurrent writers can create divergence or corruption
Every application requires both systems to write independently
Read-only clients cannot ever be redirected
explanations: Incorrect. Naming does not implement consistency control.
Correct. Ownership must follow the supported architecture.
Incorrect. That is not a universal supported mode.
Incorrect. Read routing is a separate question.

questions.prompt: A local test on the new node passes immediately after DNS cutover. What remains to be checked?
options: Actual client resolution/routing and service behavior during cache transition
Whether the new node can run the already-passed local test
Whether the old node has any inventory label
A guarantee that all DNS caches change instantly
explanations: Correct. Clients may still use the old endpoint.
Incorrect. That is existing evidence.
Incorrect. Identity matters, but it does not validate client cutover.
Incorrect. Caching prevents that assumption.

questions.prompt: A migration changes the data format so the old software cannot read it. What should the recovery plan state?
options: Any old binary can always read the new format
Renaming the database file restores compatibility
A backup label removes the need for restore testing
Rollback may be unsupported; define a verified forward-recovery or restoration route
explanations: Incorrect. That contradicts the stated incompatibility.
Incorrect. Names do not change format semantics.
Incorrect. Artifacts must be validated with the supported software.
Correct. Reversal depends on compatibility, not intention.

questions.prompt: Why test backup on the new target after refresh?
options: A successful migration is itself a permanent backup
The old backup schedule necessarily discovers every target change
Protection may still reference only the old host or omit changed dependencies
The target can never fail while under warranty
explanations: Incorrect. It is a transition, not enduring independent protection.
Incorrect. That must be verified rather than assumed.
Correct. Service migration does not automatically update every recovery process.
Incorrect. Warranty does not prevent failure.

questions.prompt: A final architecture meets redundancy requirements but the migration removes two required members simultaneously. What is missing?
options: An assumption that maintenance never overlaps faults
A transition sequence preserving the approved surviving state
Only the final healthy component count
A larger count of final healthy components
explanations: Incorrect. The plan must account for its required failure state.
Correct. End-state resilience does not make every path to it acceptable.
Incorrect. Final resources are not all available during the temporary state.
Incorrect. Those are not all available during the transition.

questions.prompt: When is the retained old system ready for retirement?
options: After its service/data role is resolved and the approved decommissioning process can proceed
Immediately after one successful target login
As soon as its hostname is removed from a slide
Whenever its front-panel light is off
explanations: Correct. Acceptance must account for lingering authority and dependencies.
Incorrect. That is incomplete functional and recovery evidence.
Incorrect. Documentation does not disable service or erase data.
Incorrect. Power state does not establish retirement readiness.

questions.prompt: An asset is marked disposed while physically awaiting sanitization in a cage. What should be corrected?
options: The serial should be deleted so the mismatch disappears
The label alone should be treated as proof of destruction
The pending media should be returned to unrestricted stock
The lifecycle/custody record must reflect the actual pending state
explanations: Incorrect. That destroys traceability.
Incorrect. An administrative status cannot establish the physical event.
Incorrect. Its data disposition remains unresolved.
Correct. Intended disposal is not completed disposal.
questions.exhibit: Synthetic custody: asset status disposed; actual location staging cage; media treatment pending; BMC still reachable.

questions.prompt: A retired host's disks are sanitized but its BMC account remains active. Which requirement remains separate?
options: Only the fact that production data interfaces are unplugged
A guarantee that power-off revokes credentials
Management identity/configuration removal or approved reassignment
The existence of disk sanitization evidence
explanations: Incorrect. The separate management path and credentials can remain active.
Incorrect. Persistent accounts can remain available later.
Correct. Media treatment does not automatically close management authority.
Incorrect. That can be complete within its own scope.

questions.prompt: Why inventory information-bearing components beyond the main disks?
options: Sanitizing one disk always resets every controller
Configuration, logs or other data can persist in separate embedded/removable components
Every component necessarily stores identical complete datasets
A motherboard label itself is a full database
explanations: Incorrect. That cannot be assumed.
Correct. The main data volume is not the only possible storage.
Incorrect. Actual persistence is model-specific.
Incorrect. Identification is not equivalent to all data content.

questions.prompt: A disposal certificate names a different serial from the asset sent. What is the correct disposition?
options: Hold closure and reconcile identity and evidence with the approved custody process
Edit the sent asset's serial to match without investigation
Accept any certificate from the provider as interchangeable
Claim the item was destroyed because a work order existed
explanations: Correct. The certificate does not yet support this asset's disposition.
Incorrect. That falsifies the identity chain.
Incorrect. Evidence must identify the relevant media/asset.
Incorrect. Intent is not execution evidence.

questions.prompt: A relocated server uses a different power-path topology. What must acceptance consider?
options: Only the server's unchanged operating-system version
Only the prior site's successful feed-loss report
An assumption that all racks have identical feeds
The new installed dependency and required failure state
explanations: Incorrect. That does not validate facility paths.
Incorrect. That report describes a different installed topology.
Incorrect. Rack arrangements can differ.
Correct. Prior-site testing does not prove the changed arrangement.

questions.prompt: What does chain of custody establish by itself?
options: That the service was successfully migrated
That all certificates and licenses were revoked
Documented possession and transfer history, not sanitization effectiveness
That every bit has been irrecoverably removed
explanations: Incorrect. Custody does not test application function.
Incorrect. Those require separate administrative actions.
Correct. Handling evidence and media treatment are distinct.
Incorrect. That requires method and outcome evidence.

questions.prompt: A little-used server supplies the recovery environment's time service. What must retirement review address?
options: Deletion of its role from the inventory
The retained recovery dependency and its replacement or approved termination
Only the host's daytime CPU average
An assumption that recovery uses no time-dependent systems
explanations: Incorrect. That hides rather than resolves the dependency.
Correct. Low normal utilization does not make the role irrelevant.
Incorrect. That can miss infrequent critical functions.
Incorrect. Authentication and event interpretation may depend on time.

questions.prompt: A factory reset restores BMC settings. What cannot be assumed without model-specific evidence?
options: That all other information-bearing media and credentials have been appropriately treated
That some supported settings changed
That the procedure should be documented
That physical identity can still be recorded
explanations: Correct. Reset scope can be narrower than retirement scope.
Incorrect. That is the stated reset action.
Incorrect. Documentation remains appropriate.
Incorrect. Identity tracking is still possible.

questions.prompt: An SSD was quick-formatted before leaving organizational control. What is missing from a sanitization claim?
options: Only a successful mount of the new empty filesystem
A guarantee that flash has no remapped or spare areas
A rule that any filesystem recreation equals every sanitization category
An approved media-appropriate method and its execution/verification evidence
explanations: Incorrect. A mount verifies filesystem accessibility, not sanitization assurance.
Incorrect. That assumption is invalid for many devices.
Incorrect. The operations provide different guarantees.
Correct. Formatting alone does not establish the required assurance.
questions.exhibit: Synthetic disposition certificate: SSD serial matches; action quick format; result success; approved sanitization method absent; verification absent; asset to leave control.

questions.prompt: A cryptographic-erasure process leaves an exported usable key copy. What is the concern?
options: The device must automatically destroy itself
All other data copies are sanitized automatically
Relevant key material remains outside the claimed deletion scope
Encryption necessarily becomes stronger with each surviving key copy
explanations: Incorrect. No such physical event follows.
Incorrect. Each copy and scope needs its own disposition.
Correct. Deleting one copy may not make protected data inaccessible.
Incorrect. Additional copies can preserve access.

questions.prompt: Why does host-visible overwrite alone need careful review on flash media?
options: A faster interface guarantees stronger sanitization
Mapping, remapped and spare areas can differ from the exposed logical address space
Flash always exposes every physical cell directly and permanently
Overwriting a filename necessarily invokes device sanitization
explanations: Incorrect. Transport speed is not assurance.
Correct. Visible addresses do not necessarily cover all relevant physical locations.
Incorrect. Translation layers can intervene.
Incorrect. Filename operations are different.

questions.prompt: A tool reports completion but the logged serial is wrong. What is the release decision?
options: Hold until the actual target and outcome are reconciled
Release the intended asset based on any successful run
Assume a matching model name is sufficient despite the serial mismatch
Assume all connected devices were sanitized together
explanations: Correct. The result does not yet establish treatment of the intended asset.
Incorrect. Success on another target is insufficient.
Incorrect. The target must be uniquely reconciled; a model can describe many devices.
Incorrect. Scope must be established by the method and record.

questions.prompt: What must be true before a sacrificial-media sanitization exercise?
options: A production backup can be borrowed without checking dependencies
The learner has answered a question correctly
The target's device name looked familiar once
The exact authorized target contains no required data and is isolated from unintended systems
explanations: Incorrect. That could destroy required recovery data.
Incorrect. Knowledge alone does not authorize a target.
Incorrect. Stable identity and current use must be verified.
Correct. Destructive practice requires a verified disposable scope.

questions.prompt: Why is the offline temporary-file restoration demo not media sanitization evidence?
options: All temporary files are inherently encrypted with validated erase keys
A Python process automatically controls every flash spare block
File operations in a temporary workspace do not validate a device-level sanitization method
It cannot demonstrate any hash comparison
explanations: Incorrect. That is not established.
Incorrect. It does not.
Correct. Its demonstrated scope is file loss and restoration only.
Incorrect. It can verify file content within its scope.

questions.prompt: A device cannot complete the selected approved sanitization method. What should happen?
options: Release it solely because it no longer mounts normally
Hold disposition and select an appropriate approved alternative or escalation
Mark it sanitized because the attempt started
Remove errors from the certificate
explanations: Incorrect. Inaccessibility through one interface is not the full assurance claim.
Correct. A failed method cannot be recorded as successful.
Incorrect. Attempt and successful outcome differ.
Incorrect. That conceals material evidence.

questions.prompt: What additional condition matters to a cryptographic-erasure claim beyond deleting a current password?
options: Suitable prior encryption and complete relevant key scope in the supported implementation
Only whether the current user password was changed
Only whether the filesystem has free space
A belief that any encryption setting proves all historical data was protected
explanations: Correct. A password action alone may not eliminate all data access.
Incorrect. A password change need not destroy the underlying data-encryption keys.
Incorrect. Free space does not establish key destruction.
Incorrect. Earlier unencrypted data and implementation details need review.

external_requirements: HW-02: stage and install a real server or storage device and retain approved rack, power, cable and handover evidence.
HW-03: perform a supported firmware update and test the applicable recovery path on authorized equipment; record unsupported rollback.
HW-04: configure supported storage and exercise a safe drive/path failure, replacement/rebuild and independent restoration.
HW-06: execute bounded representative diagnostics against preapproved limits and retest an introduced safe fault.
HW-08: complete an authorized physical FRU replacement; inaccessible component classes remain open until supervised evidence exists.
HW-10: execute and validate an approved sanitization method on sacrificial lab media with synthetic data; evidence includes custody and identity removal.
Study, question scores and offline fixtures do not close these physical gates.
